title: Chronos tiny frequency-conditioned probabilistic output View
hypothesis: A two-scalar frequency-conditioned Givens code over standardized Chronos forecast-sample shapes can improve proper probabilistic forecast quality on chronologically later, dataset-held-out ETT/Monash series beyond zero-shot Chronos and ordinary output temperature calibration, while adding negligible state and under 10% decode/postprocessing latency.
physical_object: One frozen amazon/chronos-t5-tiny checkpoint, shared across all series and frequencies.
mirror_coordinate: m=(theta_15min, theta_1h), two float32 values. For each forecast lead, orthogonalize the centered forecast sample residual against its squared residual and apply a Givens rotation by theta. Between 15-minute and hourly development frequencies, interpolate linearly in log2(hours/step); clamp outside the observed interval to the nearest endpoint.
logical_multiplicity: Frequency-conditioned probabilistic output distributions for many univariate forecast series from one frozen decoder.
prior_art_delta: Chronos already normalizes and quantizes each input series and samples probabilistic output trajectories. The candidate changes only the post-decoder distribution shape, preserving each lead's ensemble mean and variance. The matched native controls are output temperature scaling and the algebraically equivalent normalized quadratic/Hermite residual.

model.architecture: Official Chronos-T5-Tiny, 8M parameters, CPU float32 weights. Chronos quantizes real-valued series into 4096 input/output token bins; checkpoint weights themselves are not INT8 quantized. The registry wording 'quantized decoder' is interpreted as Chronos token quantization, not post-training weight quantization.

development.split: first 60% chronological rows fit development code; next 20% validate and choose the frozen grid/config; last 20% of these development files is not scored for final evidence.
development.series: all seven numeric channels, excluding date; 4 spaced fit windows and 2 spaced validation windows per channel; window targets do not overlap within each channel. Horizon 24 follows the Chronos paper evaluation table for ETT 15-minute and hourly zero-shot datasets; seasonal period for ETTm1 remains 96.

datasets.source: Chronos paper zero-shot benchmark II / Monash TSF
Chronos paper zero-shot benchmark II / Monash TSF

fresh_audit.split: Final 20% of each chosen series is the forecast-target region; forecast origins are fixed, evenly spaced, non-overlapping by horizon, and use only observations strictly preceding the target. No audit labels or forecasts are used to fit m or controls.
fresh_audit.model_pretraining_overlap: The Chronos paper lists Weather and Australian Electricity in its zero-shot evaluation benchmark. The selected source datasets and future targets are held out from this experiment's code fitting. This is not an independent re-pretraining audit.

data.split_integrity: Development uses only ETTh1/ETTm1. Audit uses different Chronos zero-shot datasets Weather and Australian Electricity, 12 predeclared Weather series and all 5 electricity series. Dataset/frequency pairs are disjoint from development. Daily Weather is outside the dev frequency interval and receives the protocol-frozen clamped hourly code.

controls: Native frequency-conditioned output temperature calibration with two float32 coefficients, fitted only on development forecasts
Native two-coefficient location/scale calibration on the two development frequencies
Normalized quadratic/Hermite residual control; this is algebraically equivalent to the one-angle Givens View after amplitude normalization and is an explicit Mirror-specificity falsifier
Seasonal-naive forecast using period 24/96 in development and period 7/48 in audit

selection.development_frequency_code: Fit theta_hour and theta_15min from train-region forecast samples using the preregistered grid [-0.60,0.60] step 0.05 radians; choose the minimum equally weighted mean empirical CRPS. Fit the two coefficients of the log-frequency temperature and the native two-frequency location/scale on the same train windows. Use the next chronological 20% only for selecting among predefined method/config variants, then freeze one candidate state.
selection.metric_primary: Empirical sample CRPS, equal-weighted across audit datasets after normalizing each dataset score by its frozen seasonal-naive CRPS.
metrics_secondary: normalized weighted quantile loss at tau=0.1,0.5,0.9
90% interval coverage and absolute coverage error
decoder and postprocessing p50/p95 wall time
selection.bootstrap: 10,000 paired block bootstrap replicates, block=one complete series; use as descriptive uncertainty, not to relax point-estimate gates.

gates.promising: Across both fresh datasets, Mirror improves normalized CRPS by at least 1.0% versus zero-shot and at least 0.5% versus the strongest native temperature/location-scale control; normalized WQL does not worsen more than 0.5%; median MASE does not worsen more than 1%; p95 added decode+View latency <=10%; complete payload includes the single shared checkpoint and all m/config state.
gates.fail: Mirror fails its quality gate on either audit dataset, or a native temperature/Hermite control matches its score within 0.1%, or the code adds no useful downstream distribution quality. An exact Hermite/Givens alias is a FAIL for Mirror-specific attribution even if the shared postprocessing is useful.
gates.not_established: Model/data execution unavailable, fewer than 8 valid selected Weather series or fewer than 4 electricity series, unrecoverable Chronos inference instability, or test split/series overlap cannot be verified.

paid_objects: all shared checkpoint inference files (model.safetensors and model/generation configs)
two float32 frequency View coefficients or native calibration coefficients
forecast sample count and generation config
storage.reporting: Report common checkpoint bytes once, then full checkpoint+method state for every method, plus incremental state bytes and source/runner code bytes separately. No claim that code-generation algorithm or checkpoint is free.

report: active generated tokens and forecast samples
compute.training: No Chronos weight updates; only development calibration codes are fit.

boundaries: One small Chronos checkpoint and two Monash zero-shot datasets; no broad time-series foundation model claim.
No unseen model architecture or frequency beyond the registered clamped extension.
The View and Hermite residual control may be algebraically identical; no Mirror-specific claim without beating the simpler control.
Chronos checkpoint weights are FP32; only the input/output series tokenizer uses quantized tokens.

amendments.reason: After protocol freeze and before any forecast metrics, checking the Chronos PA326 benchmark table showed that ETT (15-minute) is evaluated at horizon 24, not 96.
amendments.change: Correct ETTm1 development horizon from 96 to the published Chronos horizon 24; retain seasonal period 96 for daily-cycle MASE.

amendments.reason: Development metric review found that averaging per-window WQL ratios gives unstable weight to near-zero-valued ETTh1 series. Standard aggregate WQL pools the quantile-loss numerator and absolute-target denominator before division.
amendments.change: Report each dataset/series WQL as sum(quantile loss numerator) divided by the pooled sum(abs(target)) across windows; development WQL is recomputed from saved forecast samples.
